chunk-001:c004.proposition: Conscious existence, rational conversation, emotion, and participation in reality may already constitute a pervasive divine encounter rather than evidence that God is wholly absent.

orphanFallback.rationale: The cited appeal to consciousness, reason, emotion, and living in God independently advances ordinary experience as positive evidence of pervasive divine presence.

chunk-001:c008.proposition: The crucified and God-forsaken Christ does not remove every hiddenness problem but reveals a God who enters humanity's abandonment and thereby makes Christian trust possible amid divine absence.

orphanFallback.rationale: The source presents the abandoned Christ as a distinctively Christian disclosure of God's identity and as an affirmative basis for trust amid experienced absence.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-01.proposition: The Christian account of Job culminates in Christ, who bears creation's suffering and uniquely judges its ultimate cost worthwhile in light of resurrection.

orphanFallback.rationale: The source independently develops a Christian account in which God the Son assumes creation's suffering and embraces its cost because of the resurrection to come.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-06.proposition: The Trinity answers the Euthyphro dilemma because eternal other-centered divine love is neither an external standard nor an arbitrary command but goodness itself.

orphanFallback.rationale: The cited description of divine life as eternal, interpersonal, other-centered love supplies a positive Christian grounding of goodness without depending on the preceding dilemma.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-08.proposition: Naturalism cannot adequately call suffering objectively wrong, whereas Christian theism grounds moral condemnation in an objective standard of goodness.

orphanFallback.rationale: The move is already constructive: its source-grounded contrast between naturalistic description and Christian moral condemnation directly advances the comparative case for objective goodness.

chunk-003:c003-01.proposition: Modern secular human-rights discourse retains Christian assumptions about human dignity while materialism cannot adequately sustain those assumptions.

orphanFallback.rationale: The source's appeal to creator-endowed equality, inalienable rights, and membership in the human family independently advances Christian inheritance as a foundation for dignity.

chunk-003:c003-08.proposition: The controlling test for Christian moral development is conformity to scripture's Jesus-centered narrative of self-giving, world-embracing forgiveness.

orphanFallback.rationale: The source positively identifies the scriptural narrative centered on the crucified, forgiving Jesus as a prospective criterion for recognizing authentic Christian moral development.
